why_no_candidate_was_built: M3 already reproduces the reference neck and shoulder contour exactly — its fitted GLASS samples are byte-identical to the reference half-widths across all 26 sampled rows from 664 to 739, and the measured neck error is 0.00078 mean / 0.00385 max against gates of 0.006 / 0.035. Building M3S1 to make the undercut MORE pronounced would move the contour AWAY from the reference and fail the very gates it is meant to satisfy. §10 requires the undercut to come from narrowing the glass below the collar; it is already narrowed by exactly the reference amount.
reinterpretation_of_inspector_findings: The reference undercut is 8 px per side on a 343 px body — 2.3% of body width. In the photograph it reads clearly because shading and a specular edge define it. In a flat neutral silhouette with no shading, an 8 px inset is close to invisible at inspection scale. Both inspectors were therefore describing a real perceptual difference with a NON-geometric cause: legibility of a correct contour under neutral fills, not contour error.
